summary.title: What are the fundamental principles of continuous integration?
summary.one_liner: Continuous integration rests on frequent integration to a shared mainline, automated builds and tests on every commit, fast feedback, and build-once-deploy-many with config separated from code.
keywords: integrate code several times a day
takeaways: Integrate small changes into a shared mainline several times a day to reduce merge conflicts and locate regressions faster.
Automate the build and run unit, integration and functional tests on every commit, with slower checks such as coverage run less often.
Keep the build green: fix broken builds immediately and reduce flaky tests.
Build the artifact once and deploy the same binary to every environment, keeping configuration separate from code.
Continuous delivery adds a manual release step on top of CI; continuous deployment automates that step too.
summary.summary: This is a Quora question page with multiple answers, several of them repeated in the page text. The answers cover CI principles from a release manager's perspective, a list-style summary of practices (frequent commits, automated builds and tests, green builds, reproducible environments, quality gates), and an explanation of how CI relates to continuous delivery and deployment. Some answers are short, generic, or contain shallow DevOps marketing-style content, so quality varies. The most concrete material is the release-manager answer and the answer describing shared-dependency divergence as the reason for frequent integration.
